# SvelteKit 3 migration tasks, resolved

Meridian was never on SvelteKit 2. It began on the SvelteKit 3 prereleases and moved to 3.0.1 in one
commit, by hand, so `npx sv migrate sveltekit-3` had nothing to rewrite here and there are no
per-task commits. What the migration can still do for a finished project is list what it would not
decide for you: run against a copy of this one, it wrote a `MIGRATION_TASKS.md` at the project root
of the migrations that are uncommon, context-dependent or not safe to automate. This is that file,
kept as the record, with its findings resolved by hand. Every box is ticked, and under each is what
resolved it — the file and line that does the new thing, or "not affected" and why the finding was
a false positive. The findings are deliberately broad; eight of the twenty were.

The course chapter on upgrades (`migrating-a-major`) reads this file.

## Migration tasks

### Copy `page.url` before mutating it

`page.url` and its search parameters are readonly in SvelteKit 3.

- [x] `src/lib/ui/Header.svelte` — not affected. The header only reads `page.url.pathname`
      (`Header.svelte:91`) to mark the current link; nothing writes to `page.url` or its
      `searchParams`. A tab change is a link with its own `?tab=`, not an edited copy of the URL.

### Review `goto` destinations

`goto(...)` now rejects destinations that do not resolve to an application route.

- [x] `src/lib/trip/CommandPalette.svelte` — resolved. The palette's one `goto` builds its
      destination with `href()`, the project's wrapper around `resolve()` from `$app/paths`
      (`CommandPalette.svelte:53`), so it is a route by construction and a typo is a type error.
      The trip page's shallow `goto('', …)` (`TripView.svelte:344`) is this entry's own URL.

### Adjust noScroll/keepFocus usage

The options `noScroll` and `keepFocus` of `goto(...)` are merged into a single `reset` option.

- [x] `src/lib/trip/TripView.svelte` — resolved. The tab strip says `data-sveltekit-reset="false"`
      (`TripView.svelte:454`), so a tab keeps the scroll position and focus; the comment above it
      says why. No `noScroll`, `keepFocus`, `data-sveltekit-noscroll` or `data-sveltekit-keepfocus`
      remains anywhere in `src`.

### Adjust error(...) usage

Signature of `error(...)` from `@sveltejs/kit` has changed.

- [x] `src/lib/trip/TripView.svelte` — not affected. The match is `toast.error(...)` from
      svelte-sonner (`TripView.svelte:352`), not SvelteKit's `error()`. Every `error()` in the
      project passes a message string — `error(404, m.error_no_trip())` in
      `src/lib/server/access.ts:67` — which is the 3.0 signature.

### Replace `invalidateAll` with `refreshAll`

`invalidateAll` is deprecated in favor of `refreshAll`.

- [x] `src/lib/trip/CommandPalette.svelte` — not affected. The palette navigates with
      `{ replace: true }` and refreshes nothing; there is no `invalidateAll` anywhere in `src`.
      Where a refresh is wanted it is server-driven: `requested(tripBySlug, 1).refreshAll()` in
      `src/lib/remote/trips.remote.ts`.

### Review `handleError` behavior

SvelteKit 3 sends expected, validation, and rendering errors through `handleError`.

- [x] `src/hooks.server.ts` — resolved. `handleError` tells the four kinds apart
      (`hooks.server.ts:206-221`): a `validation` error gets a localised message and a warning
      naming the path, `app` and `framework` errors keep SvelteKit's status and message, and only
      `unknown` gets a correlation id and a log line. `src/hooks.client.ts` has no async hook.

### CORS for static assets in development is handled by Vite

SvelteKit no longer sets `access-control-allow-origin: *` on every static asset request in
development.

- [x] Not affected. Nothing loads this app's static assets from another origin in development.
      The one cross-origin consumer is the custom element, which reads the route API — and that
      endpoint sets its own CORS headers in every mode (`src/routes/api/route/[slug=slug].json/+server.ts`).

### `json` and `text` are deprecated

The `json(...)` and `text(...)` helpers from `@sveltejs/kit` are deprecated.

- [x] `src/routes/api/route/[slug=slug].json/+server.ts` — resolved: `Response.json(...)`
      (`+server.ts:39`).
- [x] `src/routes/api/world.json/+server.ts` — resolved: `Response.json(...)` (`+server.ts:36`).
- [x] `src/routes/healthz/+server.ts` — resolved: `Response.json(...)` (`+server.ts:30` and `:32`).

### Move adapter-node `ORIGIN` to `paths.origin`

The adapter-node `ORIGIN` environment variable is removed.

- [x] Resolved. `ORIGIN` is set nowhere — not in `.env.example`, `compose.yaml` or the
      `Dockerfile`. The public origin is `paths.origin`, fed from `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` at build time
      (`vite.config.ts:74`), and `src/env.ts` declares `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` as `static` for that reason.

### Use remote form field attributes

Remote form controls must use attributes from the current form field.

- [x] `src/lib/trip/StopDialog.svelte` — not affected. Its `<form onsubmit={save}>`
      (`StopDialog.svelte:235`) is plain HTML that calls the `addStop` / `updateStop` commands; the
      `name="kind"` on its radios groups them for the browser and is never submitted to a remote
      form.
- [x] `src/routes/(site)/explore/+page.svelte` — not affected. The match is
      `<meta name="description">`; the page's filter is an input bound to state, not a form.
- [x] `src/routes/(site)/t/[slug=slug]/settings/SettingsForm.svelte` — not affected. Like the stop
      dialog, its `<form onsubmit={save}>` (`SettingsForm.svelte:74`) calls the `updateTrip`
      command; `name="visibility"` groups two radios. Every remote `form` in the project — sign in,
      sign up, new trip, expenses, join, leave, delete — takes its attributes from
      `fields.x.as(...)`.

### Review consumers of 204 responses

SvelteKit 3 returns no body for 204 and other empty 2xx responses.

- [x] `src/routes/api/route/[slug=slug].json/+server.ts` — not affected. Its `OPTIONS` handler
      already answers `new Response(null, { status: 204 })` (`+server.ts:61`), and its only
      consumer is the browser's CORS preflight, which reads headers, never a body.

## Final verification

- [x] Review every migration task and ignore any irrelevant findings — above.
- [x] Resolve remaining `@migration-task` comments — `grep -rn "@migration-task" src` finds none.
- [x] Run the project's type checker and tests — `pnpm run verify` (check, lint, the autofixer,
      unit tests, build, bundle guard, end-to-end), the same command CI runs.
- [x] Build the project successfully — `pnpm run build`, and the Docker image in CI.
- [x] Delete this file when all migration work is complete — kept instead, moved to `docs/` and
      renamed, as the record of what the migration asked and what answered it.
